issues.source_quote: Нам не страшен серый волк, серый волк, серый волк...
issues.translation_quote: Who's afraid of the big gray wolf, big gray wolf, big gray wolf...
issues.justification: Replaces the Russian children's song with a different well-known English song; this is a plausible domestication, but the following 'Я злой и страшный серый волк' rhyme is rewritten and the reference is approximated.

issues.translation_quote: I'll rip your jaw off! / gouge your peepers out!
issues.justification: Catchphrase threat is rendered inconsistently ('jaw'/'jaws', 'peepers'), and 'Docent' speech loses the gangster idiom 'пасть' (maw/trap), weakening the recurring joke.

issues.source_quote: Те сидят там, в Средней Азии, а этот под Москвой.
issues.translation_quote: Those two are doing time in Central Asia, he's near Moscow.
issues.justification: Source says 'those' (the group, two criminals plus others implied, with Troshkin's lookalike being Bely); 'two' is added and the identification of who is where is confused.
The slang 'редиска' (a bad sort) is kept literally, so the running joke is opaque; later 'Take back the radish!' and 'Answer for the radish' lose sense in English.

issues.source_quote: Хороший человек? Забыл! Фрей-фея, действительно: Фрей-фея.
issues.translation_quote: A good person? Forgot! A mark... yes, of course: a mark.
issues.justification: 'Фрей-фея' (a distorted 'фраер') is rendered as 'mark', but 'фраер' means a sucker/square, which is not a 'good person'; the slang game of mistaken term is lost.
The joke (thieves mangling English, 'ОБХС' = anti-embezzlement police) is not explained or adapted; the untranslated acronym is opaque.

issues.translation_quote: Where'd you put the helmet, you deadbeat?
issues.justification: 'Лишенец' (deprived/outcast, insulting prison term) is flattened to 'deadbeat', changing meaning.

issues.source_quote: Сколько я зарезал, сколько перерезал, сколько душ я загубил!
issues.translation_quote: How many have I slaughtered, how many have I butchered, how many souls have I destroyed!
issues.justification: This is a parody of a famous theatrical/song line; the comic pastiche register is only roughly conveyed.

issues.source_quote: Какой же это арматурный, это слесарный. Чего ты свистишь?
issues.justification: Plausible, but 'свистишь' (lying) fits the criminal slang; minor shift. Also 'Alibakan' character speech is inconsistent.
Slang 'тики-так' (all right) is left untranslated, with no cue for English readers of its meaning.

issues.source_quote: Нехороший ты человек, Косой, злой, как собака.
issues.translation_quote: You bad man, Kosoy, mean like dog.
issues.justification: Broken-English pidgin is applied to Vasya/Ali-Baba in some places but inconsistently elsewhere (he speaks fluently in other lines), muddying characterization.

issues.source_quote: Я говорю "Москва", а ты на последнюю букву "А" - Астрахань.
issues.translation_quote: I say "Moscow", and you take the last letter "W" - Warsaw.
issues.justification: The English game adaptation uses wrong last letter (Moscow ends in 'w' in this spelling, yet the later 'D' prompt, Vorkuta, and 'А' Dzhambul no longer fit); the sequence is incoherent.

issues.translation_quote: like three poplars in an empty field
issues.justification: The title reference to a famous film is lost and 'Plyushchikha' replaced by an invented 'empty field'.
Acceptable but stilted; the Soviet-era pun on 'физкульт-привет' is only partly conveyed.

issues.translation_quote: It's gone. It was here, now it's not.
issues.justification: Ali-Baba's pidgin and Sanych's lines are mixed up; speaker voices are blurred.

issues.source_quote: Во дает! Видно он здорово башкой треснулся...
issues.translation_quote: Look at him go! He must've really cracked his head...
issues.justification: Fine, but 'Docent' is later confused with Troshkin in the translation of some lines, e.g. 'Rip your jaw off' when Troshkin pretends.
Name 'Хмырь' (shady type) is transliterated with no flavor in English.
